title: Rain & slopes
intro: How much rain makes the slopes fail: runoff (SCS curve number), shallow landslide probability (infinite slope, Monte Carlo) and the likely path of a debris flow, step by step through the storm. Load the study area as KMZ/KML to get the critical rainfall of its homes, schools, health centres and roads.

kmz.none: No study area: the grid's own extent, elements from OpenStreetMap
kmz.needsMap: Turn the map on to place a KMZ (its coordinates are WGS84) and to use the relief.
kmz.anchored: The study area places the scene: turn the map on (with relief) and build the grid.
kmz.rebuild: Rebuild the grid so it covers the study area.

timeline.label: Rain step
timeline.storm: {{mm}} mm fallen · minute {{min}} of the storm

note.susceptibility: Probability that the slope fails (FS < 1) as the rain soaks in. Purple: fails even without rain. Brown: likely debris paths and deposits. Blue: water down the gullies.
note.runoff: Rain that has run off so far, mm (SCS curve number).
note.debris: Where flows from the likely failures travel (light brown) and stop (dark brown).

view.block: Maquette (cut the block out, hide the map)

source.kmz: KMZ · {{housing}} homes · {{school}} schools · {{health}} health · {{road}} roads · {{other}} other

report.coarsened: Computed on cells {{k}}× the flood grid's, to keep it interactive.
report.outside: {{n}} placemarks fall outside the grid and are not assessed.
report.dry: {{ha}} ha fail even without rain with this soil (purple): too steep for it, usually rock or a cliff. They set no critical rain; check them on site.

table.title: Critical rainfall
table.empty: No exposed elements in the study area.
table.dry: On a slope that fails without rain

disclaimer: Indicative tool to communicate the hazard. It does not replace an official risk assessment, a site investigation or an early-warning system's own calibration.
